local_checks.result: No complete source trace; recorded as hardening, not a candidate. run_baseline.sh:34 runs `vllm serve "$@" --port $port` and the callers at lines 47 and 50-51 pass only the model, --runner, --max-model-len, --gpu-memory-utilization, --enable-prefix-caching and --reasoning-parser: no --host and no --api-key, and the clients use the placeholder key 'EMPTY' (run_baseline.sh:22, run_openevolve.py:37, run_codeevolve.py:60, run_shinkaevolve.py:52). Independently of that fact, the step from 'unauthenticated client of the API' to 'controls generated programs' is not present in source: an OpenAI-compatible client receives only responses to its own requests, and the flags passed enable no state-changing server feature (no LoRA runtime loading, no tool parser, no dev-mode endpoints). The exact missing fact for any stronger claim is a vLLM server capability, in the deployed version and with these flags, by which one API client alters completions returned to another. The separate case of a listener impersonating the endpoint on the loopback port is the candidate below.

local_checks.invariant: Only the problem evaluator can determine the metrics that evaluation.py returns to the framework and appends to EVAL_LOG; an invalid program scores 0.
local_checks.result: Does not hold in source for the 15 evaluators that import the program into the run_evaluator.py interpreter (circle_packing_rectangle_21:79, erdos_minimum_overlap:58, first_autocorrelation:67, heilbronn_convex_13:41, heilbronn_convex_14:41, heilbronn_triangle_11:58, hexagon_packing_11:195, hexagon_packing_12:195, kissing_number_11:66, min_max_distance_14_3d:35, min_max_distance_16_2d:35, second_autocorrelation:68, sums_differences:72, third_autocorrelation:61, uncertainty_inequality:109). evaluation.py:50-52 takes the last stdout/stderr line that starts with the fixed public marker, never reads process.returncode, and only rejects non-numeric or NaN scores (61-63). The evaluators catch Exception only, so program code that prints a marker line and ends the interpreter (os._exit or SystemExit), or that patches the evaluator module in place, decides the recorded score. No nonce, exit-status check, score bound or process separation is present. Returned as candidate benchmarks-evaluation/inband-metrics-marker-forgery.

local_checks.invariant: The score log EVAL_LOG (and programs/<sha>.py beside it), described as the source of all frameworks' scores, can be written only by evaluation.py.
local_checks.result: Does not hold in source. evaluation.py:46 passes the whole parent environment, including EVAL_LOG exported by run_baseline.sh:55, to run_evaluator.py; scientific_cases.py:42-44 and circle_packing_26/evaluator.py:148-150 start their children without an env argument, so every evaluated program in all 21 problems receives the log path and runs under the uid that owns the log. Returned as candidate benchmarks-evaluation/eval-log-writable-by-evaluated-program.

local_checks.invariant: Everything an evaluated program starts is terminated when its evaluation ends or its time limit expires (evaluation.py:41 states that the timeout can kill everything the child started).
local_checks.result: Does not hold in source. killpg is issued only inside the TimeoutExpired handler (evaluation.py:55-56; scientific_cases.py:47-48) and only for the original process group, so a descendant that changed session or group survives a timeout, and on the normal path (48) nothing is signalled at all, so any background process that released the stdout pipe survives a normally completed evaluation. circle_packing_26/evaluator.py:180 kills only the direct child. local_checks.invariant: The generated wrapper script, its results file and the module search path of the processes that run them are confined to a directory only the operator can write.
local_checks.result: Does not hold in source. The wrapper is created directly in tempfile.gettempdir() (evaluator.py:95) and executed as a script (148-150), which makes that shared directory the first module search path entry for the wrapper's imports of numpy, pickle and traceback (99-102); evaluation.py sets PYTHONNOUSERSITE only (28-30), not safe-path mode. The results file is a predictable sibling name in the same directory, opened without exclusive creation by the child (129) and loaded if it exists (166-168). The same pattern reaches the 15 in-process evaluators under OpenEvolve, whose program file is also created directly in the shared temp directory (openevolve/evaluator.py:259) and whose directory the evaluators insert at sys.path[0] (for example kissing_number_11/evaluator.py:65). Returned as candidate circle-packing-26-evaluator/shared-tempdir-on-module-search-path.

local_checks.invariant: program_path, which is interpolated unquoted into the generated wrapper source, cannot carry text chosen by a lower-trust principal.
local_checks.result: Holds for the audited callers. program_path is the resolved path that the framework chose (evaluation.py:36, 44): a tempfile name under OpenEvolve (openevolve/evaluator.py:259), and operator-chosen run directories with fixed file names for the other two frameworks per the glue scripts. No LLM-controlled text reaches the path. The interpolation at evaluator.py:105, 109 and 113 (and of temp_file.name at 129-139) is still unquoted, so an operator path containing a quote, backslash or brace yields a broken or different wrapper; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The wrapper child is stopped at the time limit and its temporary files are removed.
local_checks.result: Partly holds. The child is started in the evaluator's process group (evaluator.py:148-150), so the outer killpg at 60 s (evaluation.py:56) reaches it unless it changed group; that escape is part of candidate benchmarks-evaluation/time-limit-process-escape. The evaluator's own limit is 600 s (208-210, 291), longer than the outer 60 s, so its TimeoutExpired branch (178-182) is not reached under the shared harness, and that branch would kill only the direct child. When the outer SIGKILL arrives, the finally block (184-189) does not run, so the wrapper script and any results file stay in the temp directory; recorded as hardening.
